questions.q: What does the free Foundational CSPM tier of Microsoft Defender for Cloud actually provide?
options: Active runtime threat detection for every connected VM
Continuous configuration posture assessment that feeds recommendations and the Secure Score, but no security alerts
A paid vulnerability scanner for storage accounts only
Automatic enrollment in every Defender plan at no cost
questions.explain: Foundational CSPM is free and always-on, but it only assesses configuration and drives the Secure Score — it does not watch runtime behavior and never generates a security alert on its own.

questions.q: Why can two recommendations with very different severities still carry a similar Secure Score impact?
options: Secure Score ignores severity entirely and only counts recommendations
All recommendations are hard-coded to the exact same score value

Secure Score impact is based on severity AND the number of resources a recommendation affects, so a lower-severity finding touching many resources can weigh as much as a high-severity one touching few
Score impact is randomized to encourage reviewing every recommendation equally
questions.explain: Score impact is a function of both severity and affected resource count, which is exactly why sorting by raw recommendation count or score impact alone can miss the riskiest finding.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a Defender for Cloud recommendation and a security alert?
options: A recommendation is a static configuration finding; a security alert means a Defender plan detected a specific suspicious event or behavior on a monitored resource
They are two names for the exact same thing
Recommendations only apply to AWS accounts, alerts only apply to Azure
Alerts are generated by Foundational CSPM with no paid plan required
questions.explain: A recommendation says a configuration doesn't meet a best practice; an alert means an active, paid Defender plan observed actual suspicious behavior on that resource.

questions.q: A resource type has several open recommendations but no Defender plan enabled for it. What follows from that, according to this lesson?
options: The resource is fully protected because recommendations alone block attacks
That resource type can still raise security alerts through Foundational CSPM
That resource can never have open recommendations without an alert also being generated
That resource type will not generate security alerts, since alerts require an active Defender plan for that resource type
questions.explain: Security alerts only exist where a Defender plan is actively monitoring that resource type; recommendations can exist independently of any Defender plan being enabled.

questions.q: What does an "attack path" from the Defender CSPM add-on represent?
options: A single isolated recommendation with no relation to other resources
A chain connecting multiple individually-weak conditions (e.g., internet exposure, a vulnerability, and an over-privileged identity) into one exploitable sequence
A list of every Azure region where a resource is deployed
A record of every login attempt against a subscription, successful or not
questions.explain: Defender CSPM's cloud security graph derives attack paths by chaining related weaknesses together, showing the specific sequence an attacker could actually walk rather than listing unrelated findings.
